newsitem.title: USA: American Stores to buy back $550 million of shares.
newsitem.headline: American Stores to buy back $550 million of shares.

text.p: American Stores Co. said Friday it agreed to repurchase from the family of L.S. Skaggs and certain family and charitable trusts 12.2 million of its common shares at $45 apiece, or about $550 million.
American Stores, one of the nation's largest food and drug retailers, said the repurchase permits the orderly sale by the Skaggs family and trusts of their holding in the company's stock.

The company said it will finance the repurchase initially through bank lines of credit, and then through public stock or debt offerings or both over the next six to 12 months, depending on market conditions.

The company said it also agreed to file a registration statement with regulators to enable shareholders to sell between 14.7 million and 16.4 million additional shares in a secondary offering as soon as possible.
Victor Lund, chairman and chief executive of the company, said the repurchase will boost American Stores' earnings per share slightly, and not affect its capital expenditure programme.
The share repurchase and secondary offering are expected to be completed at the same time.
The selling stockholders have agreed to enter into a 10-year standstill agreement restricting purchases and sales of the company's shares, proxy fights and other actions.

American Stores, based in Salt Lake City, operates 1,695 stores in 26 states. Its principal retail operations include Acme Markets, Jewel Food Stores, Lucky Northern California Division, Lucky Southern California Division, Jewel Osco Southwest, and Osco and Sav-on drug stores.
Its stock was unchanged at $45 early on the New York Stock Exchange.
